guide:
You are grading a question-answering benchmark. Judge each item on its own.

For an "answer" item: is the model answer the same answer as any gold answer?
Count it correct when it names the same entity, value or yes/no decision, even
with different wording, extra title words, or a short explanation. Count it
wrong when it is a different entity, hedges between options, says it cannot
answer, or adds a claim that contradicts the gold answer.

For an "evidence" item: list the indexes of the gold sentences whose fact is
stated by the evidence text. A fact is stated when a reader of the evidence
alone would learn it (same entity, same claim, same date or number when the
sentence has one). Be strict: topic overlap or a generic description of the
same subject is not enough. Return an empty list when none.

Write verdicts.json as a JSON array with one object per item, in any order:
{"id": "...", "correct": true}             for answer items
{"id": "...", "supported": [0, 2]}          for evidence items
Use only ids from items.json and do not skip any item.

answers.question: After the report by Cnbc | World Business News Leader on October 6, 2023, stating that businesses selling on Amazon might opt to set non-competitive prices, did The Verge report a change or consistency in eBay's approach to pricing competitiveness in their article on October 25, 2023?
answers.model_answer: Consistency—eBay offered price matching for qualifying lower prices.

answers.question: Does the TechCrunch article that discusses the expected debut of DeepMind's next-generation chatbot Gemini by the end of the year align with the TechCrunch article mentioning Google's release of only the "lite" version known as Gemini Pro, or do they refer to different stages or versions of the Gemini project?
answers.model_answer: They refer to different stages: Gemini was expected to debut by year-end, while Gemini Pro was the lite version released first.

answers.question: Does the Fortune article claim that Sam Bankman-Fried used Caroline Ellison as a front for secret access to customer funds at Alameda Research, while the TechCrunch article alleges that Caroline Ellison took $14 billion from customers to repay debts without Sam Bankman-Fried's knowledge, or do both articles assert different levels of involvement of Sam Bankman-Fried in the misuse of customer funds?
answers.model_answer: Both assert Bankman-Fried’s involvement; TechCrunch says he instructed Ellison.

answers.question: Between the TechCrunch report on Google's AI demo involving the Gemini Ultra model and the TechCrunch report on the antitrust suit filed against Google, was there a change in the nature of the issues reported concerning Google's practices?
answers.model_answer: Yes—from AI demo credibility to alleged anticompetitive practices harming publishers.

answers.question: Between the report from Fortune published on October 4, 2023, which discussed Mark Cohen's claims about Caroline Ellison, and the subsequent reports from The Verge regarding statements made by Caroline Ellison, was there a change in the narrative concerning her role and actions as the CEO of Alameda Research?
answers.model_answer: Yes. The narrative shifted from blaming Ellison for Alameda’s failures to her testimony that Bankman-Fried directed the misuse of customer funds.

answers.question: Between the report by The Verge on Apple's defense of its Google Search deal published on September 26, 2023, and the report by TechCrunch on the class action antitrust suit against Google published on December 15, 2023, was there a change in the portrayal of Google's business practices with respect to their impact on other companies?
answers.model_answer: Yes—from a deal Apple defended as having no valid alternative to allegations that Google’s practices harm publishers’ traffic and revenue.

answers.question: Does the Fortune article claim that Sam Bankman-Fried used Caroline Ellison as a front for secret access to customer funds at Alameda Research, while the TechCrunch article alleges that Caroline Ellison took $14 billion from customers to repay debts without Sam Bankman-Fried's knowledge, or do both articles assert different levels of involvement of Sam Bankman-Fried in the misuse of customer funds?
answers.model_answer: Both articles implicate Bankman-Fried; TechCrunch says Ellison took the funds under his instruction.

answers.question: Does the Queensland Rugby Union's stance on maintaining control over their high-performance model, as reported by The Roar | Sports Writers Blog, align with Rugby Australia's efforts to centralize high-performance programs across Super Rugby teams, or are their approaches different?
answers.model_answer: They align on high-performance centralisation, but differ over control of commercial assets.

answers.question: After the report by Cnbc | World Business News Leader on October 6, 2023, stating that businesses selling on Amazon might opt to set non-competitive prices, did The Verge report a change or consistency in eBay's approach to pricing competitiveness in their article on October 25, 2023?
answers.model_answer: Consistency—eBay offers price matching on qualifying items.

answers.question: Do the articles from The Roar | Sports Writers Blog discussing The All Blacks' actions in the Rugby World Cup final and their previous encounters with Argentina both present The All Blacks as having faced challenges in their gameplay, or do they portray different situations regarding The All Blacks' performance?
answers.model_answer: Both present challenges for the All Blacks.

answers.question: Does the Queensland Rugby Union's stance on maintaining control over their high-performance model, as reported by The Roar | Sports Writers Blog, align with Rugby Australia's efforts to centralize high-performance programs across Super Rugby teams, or are their approaches different?
answers.model_answer: They align on centralising high performance, but differ over commercial control: QRU wants to retain its commercial independence.
